## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d51132be3a68d686879008ebfdf3b067b085c827`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md, AGENTS.md + scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs, scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs

Inputs read: card #31538 (body; comments 6722205630 ruling C, 6723903195 claim, 6724801860 os-dev-report), PR #31628 body and file list (4 files, every patch present, none truncated), `git diff origin/main...pr31628`, the live tree at `origin/main` and `pr31628`, and the 43 check-runs on the head. Of those, 31 are concluded (success or expected skip; `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Check PR Size`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · debt ledger` all success) and 12 were still `in_progress` at the time of this read (`Test Core 1/8`, `Test Core 2/8`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, the six `Lint ·` lanes, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`). No concluded check is red. "Every check green" is the landing condition, not this record's; the seat re-reads it before any landing.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set, `workflows` row (objectstack only).** `GOVERNED_SURFACES[workflows]` keeps `tier: H` and gains `split: { repos: ['objectstack'], reader: 'readWorkflowDiff' }` (check-governed-merges.mjs:1283). Every path-only reader (`--test`, the relay's `governedReviewPlan`, the CODEOWNERS mirror, the record face) still answers H. Only a caller that hands in a measured reading can move the row to S, and `applyWorkflowSplit` (:2085) passes every non-split row and every other repository through as the same object. **Right** — fail-closed by construction, byte-identical where no workflow path is hit.
- **Tier S reachable at the queue.** `attachWorkflowReadings` (queue-guard:2479) reads each `merge_group` row against `sha^1`; `enumerateRows` (:2433) lists `--first-parent` commits, so each row is one PR's merge commit and `^1` is the previous queue entry — the diff IS the PR's net change. `pull_request` rows read merge-base→head. Inventory of "already in use" is the merge base on both legs, so an earlier PR in the group cannot vouch for a later one's new action. **Right.** The guard workflow checks out `fetch-depth: 0` on both legs (blobless on `pull_request`; `git show` fetches blobs on demand), so `rev-parse`, `ls-tree` and `show` can answer. **Right.**
- **Fail-closed doors.** No reading / unmeasured / git throws / no base / a path the reading did not classify / an empty list / a new, deleted or non-`.yml` file / an unparseable copy / a second commit of the same PR not read / `--test` always / `--pr` off a checkout without both commits: each is H (:1996–2077, :2069–2077, queue-guard:1162). **Right** — but see ④ M1/M2: "unparseable" is narrower than the header claims, and a *parseable* copy can hide a C2 trigger.
- **Tier H by path — the six files.** Read on `main`: `release.yml` (publish + tag push), `docker-publish.yml` and `framework-build-base.yml` (`push: true`, `packages: write`), `docs-deploy.yml` (`vercel deploy`), `checklist-status.yml` (wiki push, `contents: write`), `fleet-write.yml` (App key, five write grants). **Right set.** The remaining write-holding files are covered without a path pin: `cross-repo-issue-closer.yml` is `pull_request_target` + a cross-repo PAT, and the classifier marks ANY edit to a `pull_request_target` file H (:1948); `merged-branch-reaper.yml`'s `reap`, `codeql.yml`, `stale.yml`, `pr-automation.yml`, `half-state-patrol.yml`, `merge-queue-triage.yml`, `scheduled-full-run-card.yml`, the two timings-refresh pushers: their write-token or secret-holding jobs/steps are `writeOwners`/`credentialOwners`, so any edit inside them is H (:1978–1982). Accepted.
- **Public surface.** New exports from `check-governed-merges.mjs`: `WORKFLOWS_PREFIX`, `WORKFLOW_SPLIT_RULING`, `WORKFLOW_TIER_H_FILES`, `readWorkflowTree`, `workflowUsesIdentity`, `workflowFacts`, `workflowInventory`, `workflowDiffReasons`, `classifyWorkflowChange`, `readWorkflowDiff`, `mergeWorkflowReadings`, `workflowSplitVerdict`, `applyWorkflowSplit`, `renderWorkflowSplitLines`, `pullWorkflowDiff`; `governedTierFor` and `testVerdict` gain an optional trailing `workflowDiff` (defaults preserve every existing caller). From the queue guard: `attachWorkflowReadings`. These are repo scripts, not a published package. **Right.**
- **CODEOWNERS unchanged, mirror green.** The mirror reads the row's `tier` (still H) so `/.github/workflows/` stays routed. Consequence judged in ③ B3.
- **`.github/actions/**` is not a register row** (pre-existing). The inventory counts `uses:` under `.github/actions` as "already in use" (:2035), so an ungoverned composite-action edit can introduce a third-party action that a later workflow edit then adopts at Tier S. Pre-existing gap the split makes reachable; follow-up, not this card (a new row is a ruling-sized edit). Nit N3.

### ② Semver level

The diff touches two repo scripts and two prose files; no `packages/**`, no published entry point. Label `skip-changeset` is on the PR and `Check Changeset` concluded success. `Clause-②: no` on the PR body — no narrowing of a published spec is declared and none is made. **Correct.**

### ③ Boundary flags

- **B1 (dev deviation: no assignees / no reviewers requested via MCP, seat rules 3 and 10 followed).** Posting mechanics, outside the contract judged here. Answered: no effect on the record.
- **B2 (dev flag: `scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs` `governedReviewPlan` is path-only, so a Tier S workflow PR still has approvers requested).** Read on `main`: it requests, it does not bar. An over-summon in the safe direction, outside the card's file surface. Answered: accepted deviation, follow-up card.
- **B3 (CODEOWNERS unchanged — "a request, not a barrier").** The PR body's claim holds only while no ruleset binds "Require review from Code Owners"; CODEOWNERS' own header (`.github/CODEOWNERS`, "the entry a ruleset's 'require review from Code Owners' can bind to") says such a binding is possible. With it bound, a Tier S workflow PR cannot enter the queue without an approver's review and C3 is undelivered (fail-closed, not unsafe). Card Execution 1 said CODEOWNERS "follow[s]"; it did not, by a reasoned choice (the mirror reads the row's static tier). **Escalated to the maintainer:** confirm whether the ruleset requires code-owner review on `main`; if it does, either the mirror learns the split (route `/.github/workflows/` only when the ruleset does not bind it) or Tier S for workflows is accepted as reachable only by a seat-side approval request. No grade; the maintainer's word decides.
- **B4 (card item 4, cloud and objectui).** Out of scope by order; `split.repos` names objectstack alone and the self-test pins objectui and cloud at H. Cross-repo card owed after landing. Answered.
- **B5 (open question none declared).** The PR body's "Cases biased to Tier H" list is a design statement, not an open question; it is judged in ④.

### ④ Design judgment

**Prose faces (`hits`).**

- **AGENTS.md §14 (:287–291 at the head).** Tier H now reads "every register row except `.claude/**` and Tier S workflow edits"; Tier S names "objectstack workflow edits `readWorkflowDiff` reads as Tier S, and all of `.claude/**`". Two lines edited in place, 1050 lines kept, both ≤116 chars. The clause agrees with the code: S is exactly what `readWorkflowDiff` + `workflowSplitVerdict` return S for, in objectstack only, and the whole-PR rule ("one Tier H path makes the whole PR Tier H") is honored by `landingTierOf` over the split slice (ALL-not-ANY, pinned). `check:pm-governed-prose` anchors register globs, not tier words (read on `main`), so the edit does not move its region. **Holds.** The deleted SKILL.md approval line's substance survives at AGENTS.md:288 ("authorized APPROVED review by an account in `GOVERNED_APPROVERS`, on ANY commit and not dismissed") — verified on the head tree, line 288. **Holds.**
- **.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md (:202–203 at the head).** 319 lines kept (+1 −1); the two lines are 117 and 119 bytes, under the 120 B ceiling. "本仓 `.github/workflows/**` 按 diff 定档:发布路径、C2 触发或读不出 ⇒ H,余 S(`readWorkflowDiff`)" is a faithful one-line statement of `classifyWorkflowChange`. "`.claude/**`+下行 S 面" correctly defers to the next line. The dropped line is restated in AGENTS.md:288, which the skill already points seats at. **Holds.** Nit N1: "读不出" (cannot read) is what the code promises; M1 below shows the reader reads more than it should, so the line is true of the design and not yet of the tree.

**Implementing files — the contract (ruling C, C2/C3) sentence by sentence against the code.**

C1 (workflow edits ride their own PR) is #31424 rule 3, not this diff. C3 (record PASS + green + seat lands through the queue) is the existing Tier S leg, reached by `decomposeGovernedWork` taking the tier from the reading (queue-guard:1172–1180); pinned end to end through the real recognisers. **Holds.**

C2, trigger by trigger, and the attempts to break each:

| C2 trigger | Code | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| release/publish/deploy by path | `WORKFLOW_TIER_H_FILES` :1613; rename of a pinned file lands as a NEW file ⇒ H | holds |
| added/changed `permissions:` | :1835, both directions, flow one-liners included | holds for plain spellings; **broken by M2 (b), (d)** |
| `secrets.*` reference | `WORKFLOW_CREDENTIAL` :1625, owner-keyed so a moved line is a change | holds for plain spellings; **broken by M2 (b), (c)** |
| `pull_request_target` | :1948, any edit to such a file | holds (escaped spelling falls to "trigger set changed") |
| new third-party `uses:` | identity minus `@ref` vs merge-base inventory :1951; `./` local and `docker://` handled; no inventory ⇒ H | holds; a changed `@ref` on an action already in use is S by the ruling's own words (a version bump) — accepted |
| deleted job / required-context set | :1953–1957; id loss, literal `name:` change, computed↔computed tolerated | holds |
| new `continue-on-error` | :1840, any non-`false` value incl. expressions, owner-keyed | holds for plain spellings; **broken by M2 (a)** |
| `if:` that disables a job or step | :1839, :1969–1976 — flagged only when the owner existed on the base or the job lost an owner | **broken by M1** |

**M1 — must-fix. The `if:` trigger is keyed on an attacker-chosen owner identity (check-governed-merges.mjs:1872–1880, :1969–1976).** A step's owner is `job:ID/step:KEY` with KEY = `id` ∥ `name` ∥ `uses` identity ∥ first `run` line. A head `if:` is flagged only if `a.owners.has(owner)` or the job lost some owner. One edit defeats both: rename the gate step (`name: Gate` → `name: Gate2`), put `if: false` on it, and add a dummy step `- name: Gate\n  run: echo ok`. Traced: `b.ifs` = `[job:build/step:Gate2, 'false']`, not in base; `a.owners.has('job:build/step:Gate2')` is false; `lostOwner` finds `job:build/step:Gate` still present in `b.owners` ⇒ false ⇒ not said. No invocation is dropped (the real step keeps its `run`), no credential moves if the step held none, no `coes`, names and `needs` unchanged ⇒ `reasons = []` ⇒ **Tier S**, with the gate step disabled. The same works with `id:` keys (the dummy carries the old id) and with run-keyed steps (first line `# the gate` moved onto a dummy block). This is the C2 sentence "an `if:` that disables a job or step" landing S — the ruling's own named trigger. **Fix:** any `if:` in the head not matched `(owner, text)`-for-`(owner, text)` on the base is H unless its JOB is new on the head (`!a.jobs.has(jobId)`); a new step with its own `if:` inside an existing job then goes H, which is the biased direction the header already claims. The near-miss `near-miss-a-new-job-with-a-fresh-name-and-its-own-if-is-S` stays S under that rule; the pin `near-miss-a-moved-if-that-disables-nothing-is-S` stays S because the moved `(owner, text)` pair is matched. Add a pin for the rename+dummy shape.

**M2 — must-fix. Four spellings GitHub's parser honors that `workflowFacts` does not see, so a C2 trigger lands S. All hinge on the reader modeling text, not YAML.**
(a) **Flow mappings are opaque** (:1769, :1749). `- { name: Gate, if: false, run: "…" }` is read as an item whose `value` is the flow text and whose `children` are empty; `if`, `continue-on-error`, `run`, `uses` inside it are invisible. The step keys to `(anonymous)`, the old owner is lost, but there is no head `if` fact to flag. Dropped-invocation and dropped-`uses` biases fire only if the tokens vanish from the file; a no-op line `: pnpm check:x node scripts/y.mjs` in any run block keeps them. `main`'s workflows use one-line flow mappings only as `workflow_dispatch: {}` (two files, both pinned), so refusing a flow mapping (`{`) whose text contains a guarded key (`if`, `continue-on-error`, `permissions`, `run`, `uses`, `needs`, `secrets`, `token`, `on`) — or every `{` flow mapping outright — costs nothing on this tree and closes the door. Flow sequences of flow mappings (`steps: [{…}]`) fall under the same rule.
(b) **Double-quoted escapes are not decoded** (`unquote` :1635). YAML 1.2 `"i\x66"` is the key `if`; `"permission\x73"` is `permissions`; `"${{ secre\x74s.NPM_TOKEN }}"` is a secret reference. The reader keeps the raw text, so none matches. `main` uses no `\x`/`\u`/`\U` escape in any workflow key or scalar (grepped). **Fix:** `readWorkflowTree` refuses a double-quoted scalar containing `\x`, `\u` or `\U` (fail closed), or decodes escapes before comparison.
(c) **Expression spellings** (`WORKFLOW_CREDENTIAL` :1625). The Actions expression evaluator resolves named contexts and properties case-insensitively and accepts index syntax, so `${{ Secrets.X }}`, `${{ SECRETS.X }}`, `${{ github['token'] }}`, `${{ GitHub.Token }}` all reach the credential; the regex is case-sensitive and dot-only. **Fix:** `/\bsecrets\b|\bgithub\s*(?:\.\s*token\b|\[\s*['"]token['"]\s*\])/i`. Same `/i` for `WORKFLOW_RISKY_LINE`'s `OS_` family is harmless.
(d) **Indicator-led lines are swallowed as scalar continuations** (:1773). A line that is not a key, item or readable value becomes a continuation of `last` whenever it is deeper and `last` has no children — so `? permissions` / `: write-all` (an explicit key, honored by GitHub's YamlDotNet-based reader) becomes the job node's `value`, and the following `runs-on:` lines are then attached as that node's children without complaint. A node with both a scalar value and children is not YAML; the header's "a line that is neither a key, an item nor a continuation" refusal is narrower than claimed. **Fix:** a continuation may not start with a YAML indicator (`? : - , [ ] { } # & * ! | > ' " % @ \``), and `attach` refuses a child on a node whose `value !== ''`.
Each of (a)–(d) is a one-site change in the reader or the regex and a pin apiece; the fail-closed philosophy the header states is the right one, the tree just does not yet meet it.

**S1 — should-fix. An ADDED `needs:` is not read (:1955 reads only a lost `needs:`).** A job whose dependency is skipped is itself skipped, and a skipped required check is green to branch protection. `needs: [opt-in-job]` on a required job, where `opt-in-job` carries `if: contains(labels, 'x')`, turns the required job off with no `if:`, no `continue-on-error`, no name change ⇒ S. C2's literal list does not name `needs:`; its purpose ("a dropped required job … turns a check off while CI still reads green") does. The header already biases a *lost* `needs:` to H; the added direction is the dangerous one. **Fix:** any change to a job's `needs:` set on an existing job is H.

**Nits (no contract effect; prose or follow-up only).**
- **N1** SKILL.md:203 "读不出 ⇒ H" and the header's "Fail closed: a copy the line reader cannot parse" (:502–507 of the header block) describe the fixed design; true once M2 lands.
- **N2** `run:`/`shell:` text edits are S by C3 unless a token is dropped or a RISKY pattern is added; `echo "pnpm check:x"`, `|| :` and `shell: bash {0}` (no `-e`) slip past the biases. The ruling makes them S and the record reviewer the control; worth a line in the header's "biased" list as a known limit, not a fix on this head.
- **N3** `.github/actions/**` is ungoverned and feeds the "already in use" inventory (:2035) — a follow-up card to add it as a register row or exclude it from the inventory.
- **N4** `WORKFLOW_CREDENTIAL`'s jsdoc "wherever it is spelled" overstates until M2 (c).

**Queue guard, sentence by sentence.** `attachWorkflowReadings` imports the one reader (never a second classifier), reads `^1` on `merge_group` and the merge base on `pull_request`, caches one inventory per run, marks an unresolved parent UNMEASURED; `decomposeGovernedWork` merges per-PR readings with H and UNMEASURED winning; `renderGuardVerdict` prints the split lines under the entry. Each agrees with the header's new paragraph (:338–343) and with AGENTS.md's clause. The `pull_request` leg's blobless checkout fetches ~35 workflow blobs on demand for the inventory — slower, advisory leg, exit 0; not a finding. **Holds**, modulo M1/M2 which live in the shared reader.

**Self-tests (read, not run).** 45 + 30 pins, battery floors 36/30, one pin per C2 trigger and the named near-misses. The pins encode the design's intent faithfully; none exercises a renamed-owner `if:`, a flow-mapped step, an escaped key, a case-variant context or an added `needs:`, which is why the holes above are green.

**Verdict reasoning.** The register change, the queue plumbing, the fail-closed doors, the six pinned files and both prose faces are right and agree with the ruling. The reader beneath them lets two named C2 triggers (`if:` on an existing step; `permissions`/`secrets`/`continue-on-error` in a spelling GitHub honors) land Tier S on a one-file, one-PR edit. A must-fix is a FAIL.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-hzucdt`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QsR2jT34CXs5fCn3BDirZw`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `87f686fcdd439f2dece2485fd900cf597782b06d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md, AGENTS.md + scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs, scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs

Delta review of the FAIL record 6724981811 (head `d51132be`). Inputs: card #31538 with every comment (the dev's rework report is 6725303510), the patched PR body, the net diff against `main` (`69244406`) at this head, the incremental diff `d51132be..87f686fc`, the live tree, and the 42 check-runs on the head. Of those, 35 are concluded — every one success or an expected skip (`Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Type Check · source gates`, `PR-body guards`, `Check PR Size` all success) — and 7 were `in_progress` at read time (`Test Core 1/8`, `2/8`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`). None red. "Every check green" is the landing condition, re-read by the seat before any landing.

### ① Derived judgments

- **What moved since `d51132be`.** Commit `d9c3c22d` touches `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` (+76/−31, the reader, the classifier, the header and 16 new pins) and `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` (one line, N1). Merge `87f686fc` brings `main` `69244406` in; on the four scope files `main` changed only SKILL.md:313 (the `Metadata-protocol:` template line, #31619's own edit), and the merge carries exactly that line — nothing from `main` touched the two scripts or AGENTS.md, and no conflict resolution altered the PR's hunks. The queue guard is byte-identical to the reviewed head. **Right.**
- **Accept set unchanged in shape.** The row still keeps `tier: H` with `split.repos = ['objectstack']`; readers without a reading still answer H; the refusals grew (flow mapping, escape, indicator, valued parent) and every refusal is H. The S side can only shrink under this delta. **Right.**
- **Live-tree compatibility of the new refusals (read, not run).** The flow-mapping refusal strips `${{ … }}` non-greedily before testing for a brace; the two live lines that carry `format('…{0}…')` inside an expression (`framework-build-base.yml:60`, `publish-smoke.yml:63`) are spanned by that strip because their inner `}` is followed by `'`, not `}`. `workflow_dispatch: {}` (two files) is the one allowed mapping. No `main` workflow carries a `\x`/`\u`/`\U` escape, an explicit `?` key, or a `github[` / `toJSON(github)` spelling. Block scalars are not value-checked, so JS/shell braces under `run: |` are untouched. The dev's "32 workflows and 3 actions parse, 0 differ from the `yaml` lib" is consistent with what the tree shows; not re-run here. **Right.**
- **Public surface.** No export added or removed this round; `WORKFLOW_CREDENTIAL` is module-private. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: repo scripts and prose only, `skip-changeset` on the PR, `Clause-②: no`, `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head. **Correct.**

### ③ Boundary flags

- **B1, B2, B4** — unchanged from 6724981811 (answered: posting mechanics; the relay's path-only over-summon is an accepted deviation with a follow-up; item 4 is a cross-repo card).
- **B3 (CODEOWNERS / "Require review from Code Owners")** — the tree does not answer it: CODEOWNERS is unchanged and still routes `/.github/workflows/`, and no ruleset is readable from the tree. **Stays an escalation to the maintainer**, as before. Not a grade.
- **B6 (PR body).** The dev's report says the body was stale; the body now on the PR carries the 604-assertion count, the "any case, dot or index" credential wording and the new `if:`/`needs:` sentences — it matches the tree I read. Noted, not judged (the tree is judged, not the body).

### ④ Design judgment

**Prose faces (`hits`).**

- **AGENTS.md** — unchanged since the reviewed head (net vs `main`: the same two in-place edits at :287 and :290; 1050/1050 lines). The clause "Tier S workflow edits … `readWorkflowDiff` reads as Tier S" is true of a reader that now refuses more and says S for less. **Holds.**
- **SKILL.md** — net vs `main`: one line removed (the approval line, surviving at AGENTS.md:288, verified again on this head), one line reworded (:202, 117 B), one line added (:203, now `- 本仓 .github/workflows/** 由 readWorkflowDiff 定档:发布路径、C2 触发、拒读或未读 ⇒ H,余 S。`, 119 B). 319/319 lines, the ratchet's ceiling (`check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs:413`). Lines over 120 B in the file are the pre-existing template block (:53–166, :291–318), none touched by this PR; `main`'s own :313 edit is among them and is `main`'s. "拒读或未读 ⇒ H" (refused or unread ⇒ H) is now the exact behaviour: `classifyWorkflowChange` makes a refusal H and `workflowSplitVerdict` makes no reading H. **Holds; N1 closed.**

**The round-one findings, each against the code at this head.**

- **M1 — closed for the shape found; see D1 for the shape that remains.** :1989–1994: every head `if:` not matched `(owner, text)` on the base is H unless its job is absent from `a.jobs`. The renamed-step-plus-dummy edit now says `an if: added or changed in a job that already ran: job:build/step:Gate2` (pin `⛔ M1-a-renamed-gate-step-…`), the `id:` re-key likewise, and a new step with its own `if:` inside an existing job is H (the biased direction the header claims). The moved-`if` near-miss stays S because the pair matches; the new-job near-miss stays S. Bypass attempts: changing the job id makes a deleted job (H); a job-level `if:` on an existing job is H; a workflow-level owner is H. One door is left open by the carve-out itself — D1.
- **M2 (a) — closed.** `unreadableValue` :1678–1679 refuses any value holding a brace after stripping expressions and quoted scalars, `{}` excepted; applied to kv values and to item/scalar text alike, so `- { … }`, `steps: [{ … }]` and a multi-line `{` all refuse. Control: `merge_group: {}` and `${{ inputs.os || 'ubuntu-latest' }}` parse (pin `M2a-…-still-parse`). A `}}` inside a quoted string inside an expression would refuse — the H direction, acceptable.
- **M2 (b) — closed.** :1749 refuses a line whose double-quoted scalar carries `\x`, `\u`, `\U`, `\N`, `\L`, `\P` or `\_`, key or value, anywhere on the line. Those are the only YAML escapes that spell a character beyond the C0/quote set, so no remaining escape can spell `if`, `permissions`, `secrets` or `token`. Single-quoted scalars have no escapes; a quoted scalar spanning lines was already refused.
- **M2 (c) — closed for the five spellings; see D2.** :1633 `/\bsecrets\b|\bgithub\s*(?:\.\s*token\b|\[\s*['"]token['"]\s*\])/i`, five pins (`Secrets.`, `SECRETS.`, `github['token']`, `GitHub.Token`, `github . token`). `secrets[...]`, `toJSON(secrets)` and every case of `secrets` match.
- **M2 (d) — closed.** :1792 refuses a would-be continuation led by any of `? : - , [ ] { } # & * ! | > ' " % @ \``; `attach` :1717–1725 returns false when the parent (root excepted) already holds a scalar value, and both call sites fail the read. `? permissions` / `: write-all` now refuses at the `?` line; `name: Build Core` followed by a deeper `if: false` refuses at the child.
